prompt: A firm in a perfectly competitive industry is currently producing at a level where price equals $40, average total cost (ATC) equals $45, and average variable cost (AVC) equals $35. The firm should most likely:

options.A: Shut down immediately because it is losing money.
options.B: Continue operating in the short run but exit the industry in the long run.
options.C: Increase output until price equals ATC.

explanation: In the short run, a firm should operate as long as price (P) exceeds average variable cost (AVC), because doing so covers variable costs and contributes something toward fixed costs. Here P = $40 > AVC = $35, so shutting down would increase losses (the firm would still owe fixed costs of $10 per unit but receive nothing). However, since P = $40 < ATC = $45, the firm is losing money and will exit in the long run if prices do not improve. Option A is incorrect — short-run shutdown requires P < AVC. Option C is incorrect — output decisions in perfect competition follow P = MC, not P = ATC.
